title: Normalization and Formatting
definition: Normalization converts equivalent inputs to a consistent internal form, while formatting converts internal values into an intended output representation.
purpose: Reduce representational variation internally while preserving output requirements at system boundaries.
history: Software systems normalize varied external representations for consistent processing and format internal values for humans or other systems.
mental_model: Normalization chooses one internal shape; formatting creates a boundary-specific view without changing the underlying meaning.
analogy: Different spellings are filed under one catalog form and later printed in a chosen display style; the analogy fails when normalization destroys meaningful distinctions.
industry_notes: Store stable domain representations and format at output boundaries; treat Unicode and locale rules as explicit policies.
ai_notes: AI normalization suggestions must be tested for cultural, Unicode, identity, and data-loss assumptions.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to distinguish trim, validation, normalization, transformation, and formatting.
exercise_candidates: Design canonical and display forms for a user record
